# `nlink-lab kill`

Stop tracked background processes: TERM, then KILL after a grace period; or send one signal with `-s` (`STOP`/`CONT` freeze and thaw a process in place).

```bash
sudo nlink-lab kill 4242 4243
sudo nlink-lab kill -s STOP 4242
```

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Stop tracked background processes (TERM, then KILL), or send them a signal (`-s STOP` freezes one in place)

Usage: nlink-lab kill [OPTIONS] <PIDS>...

Arguments:
  <PIDS>...
          The tracked processes to stop (PIDs `spawn` printed)

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

  -s, --signal <SIGNAL>
          Send this signal instead of the TERM-then-KILL sequence: TERM, KILL, STOP, CONT, HUP, INT, USR1, USR2 (with or without the SIG prefix). STOP/CONT freeze and thaw a process in place -- a "TCP answers, application is dead" peer for resilience tests

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
